title: Optimizing Flu Vaccine Planning at NorthShore University HealthSystem
abstract: Stan Kent, vice president of pharmacy at NorthShore University HealthSystem, is faced with the challenge of seasonal planning for the influenza vaccine. The supply received by the multilocation healthcare system is unreliable in terms of timing and quantity. As part of improved planning, Kent is contemplating a new contract with NorthShore's major supplier of flu vaccines. The options under consideration include fixing either the date of delivery or the quantity delivered. The main decision involved in either option would be how much vaccine to order. The case also provides details about the seasonal influenza epidemic in the United States, illustrates operational complexities of the U.S. flu vaccine supply chain, and provides a brief description of the various channels used to distribute flu vaccine to end consumers. The main objective of the case is to illustrate supply chain decision making when there is an unreliable supply (in contrast to the usual case of uncertain demand). A secondary objective is to make students think about appropriate internal (within sector) and external (other sectors) benchmarks to evaluate the performance of a health commodity supply chain.

summary.oneLiner: This case explores managing supply chain uncertainty by analyzing trade-offs in ordering strategies for seasonal flu vaccines with unreliable supply.
summary.overview: NorthShore University HealthSystem faces significant challenges in planning for seasonal flu vaccines due to inconsistent delivery timing and quantities from suppliers. The case focuses on how managers can optimize ordering decisions by choosing between fixed-date or fixed-quantity supply contracts. It highlights the complexities of healthcare supply chains where the primary hurdle is unpredictable supply, rather than the more common issue of uncertain demand. Students are encouraged to use performance benchmarks to evaluate how effectively the system delivers vaccines to patients.
summary.question: How can healthcare managers optimize vaccine procurement strategies when faced with unreliable supply timing and quantity?

findings: The case illustrates that supply chain decision-making in healthcare is significantly complicated by unreliable supply.
Performance in health commodity supply chains can be evaluated by identifying appropriate internal and external benchmarks.
summary.whyItMatters: The case helps managers understand how to structure supply contracts to mitigate risks associated with volatile and unreliable upstream supply chains.
